hypothesis: Within matched pairs of an oceanic island and a continental area of equal size and similar latitude and climate, the island has far fewer native species, and this holds across taxa (birds and vascular plants), so it is not explained by physical conditions.
pass_criterion: Using a sampling-standardised estimate of native species richness (coverage-based rarefaction at sample coverage 0.9, or Chao1 where coverage is lower), the island/continent richness ratio has a median ≤ 0.50 over at least 15 matched pairs. The island has lower richness in ≥ 80% of pairs. Both results hold separately for Aves and for Tracheophyta. The ratio is also still < 0.67 after restricting to continental windows whose climate matches the island's (same Köppen class, or mean annual temperature within ±2 °C).
fail_criterion: In either taxon, the median island/continent ratio is > 0.80, or fewer than 60% of pairs show lower island richness. A result in the intermediate zone (median 0.50–0.80, or 60–80% of pairs lower) counts as not supporting 'far fewer'. If the climate-matched ratio is ≥ 0.67 while the unmatched ratio is ≤ 0.50, the 'not explained by physical conditions' clause fails.
interpretation: 'Oceanic islands' means islands never connected to a continent (volcanic or coral). Examples are Hawaii, the Galápagos, the Azores, the Canaries, Mauritius, Réunion, St Helena, Tristan da Cunha, Fiji, Samoa, Society Islands, Marquesas and Juan Fernández. Continental islands are excluded. 'Equal area' means an equal-area polygon (geometry filter) placed on a nearby mainland at the same absolute latitude ±5° and in the same climate class. 'Species of all kinds' is operationalised as two well-recorded taxa, birds and vascular plants, as a proxy for all taxa. 'Physical conditions' means latitude and climate matching. Modern reinterpretation: the claim becomes the island species–area relationship, with richness measured from georeferenced occurrence records restricted to native or unspecified establishmentMeans and rarefied to equal sampling coverage. Island areas and Köppen classes must come from outside GBIF (e.g. polygons and climate rasters). The GBIF occurrence records supply only the species counts. Raw record counts are not used, because sampling effort is uneven.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (occurrence search and download API; Aves and Tracheophyta, filtered by geometry and establishmentMeans)
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF serves open occurrence records through its API and downloads, with fields taxonKey, speciesKey, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, establishmentMeans, island, countryCode, basisOfRecord and year. Species counts can be computed inside any island or mainland polygon via the geometry filter. Records can be restricted to native taxa (establishmentMeans = NATIVE or unset, with known introduced species excluded). Each custom download receives its own DOI, which the final analysis should cite. The portal itself has no single DOI, so the DOI is null here.
